title: Model Artifact Supply Chain and Image Attestation Spec
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview
---
This spec defines the minimum supply-chain, provenance, and image attestation requirements for model artifacts and runtime images used in Redwood Private (VPC and on‑prem) deployments. Goal: ensure customer and Redwood operators can verify origin, integrity, license, and reproducibility of model weights, associated artifacts (tokenizers, quantization tables), and runtime container images before they are accepted into a private deployment.

Key principles
- Cryptographic origin and integrity guarantees for every artifact entering the operator-managed runtime.
- Reproducible build metadata (provenance) so models and images can be rebuilt or audited.
- Minimal manual trust: automated gates where possible (signature verification, vulnerability scanning, policy evaluation).
- Audit evidence and retention aligned to compliance requirements.

Scope
- Model weight files (float, quantized), tokenizers, config manifests, calibration/quantization profiles.
- Container images that include runtime binary + pinned kernels and env.
- Delivery mechanisms: artifact registry (OCI), signed tarball over HTTPS, or offline airgap bundles.
- Integration points: Private Operator, Field Installer, E2E acceptance tests, SRE runbooks.

Requirements summary (top-level)
1) All artifacts must include a signed provenance statement that contains: SHA256 digest, builder identity, build timestamp (UTC), build recipe hash, source control commit or manifest ID, and license declaration. Supported formats: SLSA provenance v1 or a JSON provenance envelope conforming to Redwood schema.
2) Container images and OCI artifacts must be signed with cosign (or equivalent) and verified by the operator at intake time.
3) Private deployments must support hardware-backed key verification (customer KMS/HSM OR Redwood-managed KMS for hosted delivery) and key rotation policies documented below.
4) CVE scanning must be performed against runtime images and a policy decision made prior to acceptance (see policy table).
5) Offline airgap bundles must include an attestations folder with signed manifests and an integrity index file (signed).

Example provenance JSON (textual example)
{
  "_example": "This is an example provenance blob; production artifacts must be signed and attached separately. Replace fields with real values."
}

Provenance fields (required)
- artifact_name: canonical name used in deployment manifest (string)
- digest: sha256:... (string)
- builder_id: email or key ID of build system (string)
- builder_type: e.g., GitHub Actions, BuildFarm v2 (string)
- build_timestamp: 2026-07-01T12:34:56Z (string)
- recipe_hash: SHA256 of build recipe or Dockerfile (string)
- source: repo_url@commit OR manifest-id for closed-source (string)
- license: SPDX identifier or custom license text (string)
- artifact_class: model|tokenizer|quant-table|runtime-image (string)
- additional_metadata: comma-separated list of short key=value pairs (string)

Image signing and verification (operator workflow)
1) Intake: artifact pushed to customer-provided OCI registry or delivered via signed tar. Intake job records registry URL and digest.
2) Verification: run cosign verify --key [public-key] <image-ref> and reject if verification fails. For cosign transparency log integration, also run cosign verify --rekor-url=<url> --cert-identity-regexp=...
3) Provenance check: extract provenance blob (OCI ref: <image>@sha256:...:provenance) and validate required fields present and consistent with manifest.
4) Vulnerability policy: run Redwood CVE scanner v2.1 (or customer-provided) and compare to policy (see table).
5) Acceptance: operator marks artifact ACCEPTED and stores verification evidence in deployment audit bucket with retention tag.

Acceptance policy table (text)
- Severity >= 9.0 : BLOCK (must fix and rebuild)
- 7.0 <= Severity < 9.0 : REVIEW_REQUIRED (security owner signoff)
- 4.0 <= Severity < 7.0 : WARN (operator may accept with justification)
- < 4.0 : ACCEPT
- Kernel/OS packages EOL: BLOCK unless mitigation documented

Airgap / offline bundle requirements
- Bundle layout (top-level): /artifacts/, /attestations/, /index.sig
- index.json: lists artifacts with file path, sha256, size, and provenance ref. index.json must be signed with cosign and index.sig is the detached signature.
- Offline attestation: include cosign signature blobs (*.sig) and the builder certificate chain in /attestations/certs/.
- Installer verification steps (operator-run): verify index signature, verify each artifact digest, verify each cosign signature using trusted CA roots (customer or Redwood CA).

Customer-managed KMS / HSM guidance
- For high-security customers, keys used to sign build artifacts should be stored in the customer KMS/HSM. The operator accepts only key IDs (KMS URI) listed in the deployment spec.
- Key proof model: customer publishes a public key thumbprint to the deployment manifest. Operator uses that to verify signatures.
- Rotation: if a key rotation occurs, a migration window must be provided. New signed artifacts must be provided and re-verified before cutover. Old artifacts remain accepted for 72 hours unless explicitly revoked.

Reproducibility and rebuild policy
- Builds must be described such that an independent rebuild yields the same digest for deterministic artifacts (models trained deterministically or quantized via a documented process).
- For non-deterministic training outputs, the provenance must include the training dataset snapshot (or dataset manifest) and training hyperparameters. In these cases we require additional acceptance testing (see Acceptance Tests section).

Operator acceptance tests (automated)
1) Digest verification: compare declared digest with computed sha256.
2) Provenance signature check: validate signature and certificate chain.
3) Minimal smoke inference: run a short deterministic inference (10–20 tokens) against a canned prompt to ensure runtime compatibility.
4) KV-policy alignment: verify artifact_class and quantization profile match runtime capability.
5) CVE check & license scan: ensure no blocked CVEs and license is compatible with customer policy.

Failure modes and rollback guidance
- If verification fails during intake: mark artifact REJECTED, alert field operator, and request resubmission. Do not proceed with deploy.
- If a signed artifact is later revoked (compromise discovered): operator triggers evacuation plan for tenant routes using that artifact and fall back to last-known-good artifact. See 'evacuation and rollback checklist' below.
- Rollback checklist (rapid):
  1) Pause new traffic to affected model route.
  2) Promote last-known-good image by digest (operator API: /deploy/promote?image_digest=sha256:...)
  3) Verify smoke tests pass on promoted artifact.
  4) Run security postmortem and preserve audit evidence (signatures, rekor entries, logs).

Evacuation and fallback patterns
- Graceful degrade: switch to quantized smaller variant in a different artifact if performance/latency allows.
- Regional fallback: route traffic to hosted Redwood model variant for short-term continuity when private artifact is revoked and customer cannot provide replacement quickly. This requires pre-approved contract clause.

Audit evidence storage
- Evidence items: artifact digest, cosign verification output, provenance blob, CVE scan report, acceptance test output, operator identity that approved acceptance.
- Retention: default 2 years for enterprise customers; retention can be extended per compliance needs. All evidence stored in an encrypted S3 bucket (or customer-provided bucket) with immutable object lock if required.

Operator API snippets (examples)
- Verify image (local check): cosign verify --key /keys/deploy.pub registry.example.com/customer/model:20260701
- Verify provenance blob: cosign verify-blob --key /keys/deploy.pub --blob provenance.json provenance.sig
- Compute digest: sha256sum model-v1.q8.bin

Developer / Build pipeline guidance
- Builders should:
  - Embed the build recipe and an explicit recipe_hash in provenance.
  - Push images to an OCI registry with cosign signatures anchored to a builder key.
  - Publish provenance to a signed CAS (referenceable by digest).
  - Include a model-card (human readable) and machine-readable manifest next to artifacts.

Machine-readable manifest fields (required)
- name, version, artifact_class, digest, provenance_ref, license, recommended_runtime, quant_profile, expected_disk_bytes, expected_gpu_bytes

Operational runbook excerpts (for SREs and Field Operators)
- Intake failure:
  1) Check cosign verify output for the signature error. Common causes: missing public key, rekor mismatch, misplaced certificates.
  2) If missing public key: request KMS key id and public key file; add to operator's trust store after verification.
  3) If provenance missing fields: escalate to build-team contact in provenance blob (builder_id).
- Revocation handling: follow rollback checklist above and notify security/compliance teams.

Open questions and future work
- Automating dataset snapshot verification for non-deterministic training outputs.
- Adding a ledgered transparency log for model provenance (beyond rekor) to support cross-customer audits.
- Integrating third-party SBOM tools for model dependencies.

Appendix: Quick acceptance checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Artifact digest matches declared sha256
- [ ] Cosign signature verified against trusted key
- [ ] Provenance blob present and fields validated
- [ ] CVE policy evaluated and decision recorded
- [ ] Minimal smoke inference passed
- [ ] Audit evidence stored with retention tag

Notes on terminology
- "Artifact" refers to any file required to run a model (weights, tokenizers, quant tables, runtime images).
- "Provenance" is the signed metadata describing how the artifact was produced.
- "Acceptance" means operator has verified and recorded evidence allowing artifact to be used in production routes.
